# Helix Impulse

> Helix Impulse is a team-based marketing and strategy business simulation for universities, business schools and professional training programs – built by educators, for educators. Participants manage virtual companies, develop products, define their market positioning and make strategic marketing decisions, competing for customers and market share over several rounds.

Helix Impulse is developed by Helix Impulse GbR (Niestetal, Germany). The founders have taught with business simulations in higher education for more than 20 years. The guiding idea: keep the strategic decisions that matter and remove unnecessary complexity – a focused simulation with an intuitive interface that is easy to prepare, explain and integrate into teaching.

## Key facts

- Type: web-based marketing and strategy business simulation (participants only need a web browser; nothing to install)
- Audience: lecturers and professors at universities and business schools; professional training for companies is coming soon
- Course formats: intensive courses, seminars across the semester, business school programmes (bachelor's, master's, MBA, executive education)
- Teams: between 2 and 10 teams per simulation, each running its own company; recommended 4–6 teams of 3–6 students per market
- Timing: one full round fits a 90-minute session; an intensive week covers 8–12 rounds
- Best fit: from the second or third year of a bachelor’s degree, or at master’s level
- Rounds: chosen by the educator; the number of fiscal years varies by course, with recommendations for different formats
- Educators receive: introduction videos, teaching materials and documents, recommendations for their course format and support in the background
- Languages: website in English and German

## Pages

- [Home](https://www.heliximpulse.com/): overview, teaching formats, team, FAQ and contact form
- [Startseite (Deutsch)](https://www.heliximpulse.com/de/): German version of the home page
- [Tutorials](https://www.heliximpulse.com/tutorials.html): video tutorials on the simulation (welcome, target groups, marketing, production, sales, lab, research, controlling, finance)
- [Teaching guide](https://www.heliximpulse.com/teaching-guide.html): how to teach with a business simulation – experiential learning (Kolb), course formats (90-minute seminar with one round per session, five-day intensive week with 8–12 rounds), team sizes (typically 4–6 teams of 3–6 students per market; parallel markets for larger groups) and classroom setup
- [Legal notice](https://www.heliximpulse.com/impressum.html)
